html:
European buyers are not only buying the product — they are underwriting the quality of your evidence. The Supplier Evidence Review maps the gap between what the buyer needs to verify and what your operation can currently prove with controlled documentation: questionnaires, contract clauses, CBAM data requests, EUDR traceability, compliance and financing due diligence.

This is advisory work. It is not an audit, certification, legal opinion, emissions verification or a guarantee of buyer acceptance — and every deliverable states that boundary.

Where weak evidence costs money

Procurement risk

Fragmented documents force the buyer to rebuild your evidence file internally. Onboarding slows, review cycles stretch, confidence drops — before anyone says "no".

Contract risk

Warranties, audit rights, data duties and termination triggers all require proof. If the operation cannot support the claim, the contract becomes risk transfer — onto you.

P&L risk

Weak evidence shows up as pricing pressure, delayed renewals, reduced volumes and harder financing conversations. Revenue exposure starts quietly.

What the review does

  1. Exposure mapping. Your real buyer requests, regulations, contract clauses and commercial deadlines — not a generic ESG checklist.
  2. Evidence file reading. Documents, records, declarations, custody files, product data and audit trails, read the way a European procurement or compliance team reads them.
  3. Gap register. Unsupported claims, weak evidence, missing owners and documentation gaps — each with an owner, a date and a source.
  4. Executive risk reading. A board-usable view for procurement, legal, compliance, customs and finance: what is defensible today, what is not, and what that means commercially.
  5. Prioritised next-step plan. What to fix first to reduce approval friction — before the buyer controls the timeline.

Three formats, one discipline

No price list — every engagement is scoped case by case, on the shape of your operation, with a written proposal.

30-Day Diagnostic

The fastest useful answer: what the buyer is likely to ask, what you can prove, partially prove or cannot prove, and what to fix first. One supplier, one exposure map, one prioritised register.

Full Evidence Review

The complete engagement: exposure mapping, document-by-document reading, gap register with owners, executive risk reading and the board-readable file your buyer's committee can actually use.

Continuous Management

The retainer that keeps the file decision-ready all year — so the next request is an export, not an emergency. See Continuous Evidence Management.

When to activate

A questionnaire arrived

Procurement asks for supplier proof. You need a controlled response before scattered documents signal weak governance.

A data request arrived

CBAM emissions data or EUDR origin and geolocation. You need classification, site evidence and document governance — mapped to the actual request. For the dedicated tracks, see the CBAM Review and the EUDR Review.

A contract is on the table

Clauses request audit rights, data duties and warranties. You need to know what you can prove before signing — see the Contract Clause Review.

The deliverable: a buyer-readiness evidence map — what must be proved, which documents exist, which gaps remain, which claims are weak, which clauses may create liability, and which next steps to prioritise. Graded against the published SEMM framework, so supplier, buyer and advisor talk about the same file with the same words.

Why Villanova ESG

✓ 18 technical reports with DOIs on Zenodo  ·  ✓ Listed on ECESP — the European Commission's Circular Economy Platform  ·  ✓ The founder runs a documented Brazilian reverse-logistics operation since 2011 — the person grading a chain-of-custody record has actually run one.

Is not: an audit, an EcoVadis-style self-declared score, a site certification, or a promise of buyer approval.

Questions we hear first

Is this an audit or certification?

No — and be wary of anyone who says yes. We produce advisory assessments with a published methodology. Certification is a different, accredited activity.

How fast can it start?

The scoping conversation ends with a written proposal; a 30-day diagnostic starts from the documents you already have. First reply within 1 business day.

What does it cost?

Engagements are scoped case by case — cohort size, depth and calendar drive the work. There is no price list, by design: the product is specific to your exposure.

Received a request like this? Send it as it arrived — we reply with the priority risks and the recommended next step, within 1 business day.
